newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan navy steps up patrols against illegal aliens.
newsitem.headline: Japan navy steps up patrols against illegal aliens.

text.p: Japan's navy said on Thursday that it would increase aerial patrols of sea routes often used by Chinese boats carrying illegal immigrants in an effort to stem a sudden jump in migrant smuggling this year.
A navy spokesman said the navy would increase patrol sorties by its fleet of 100 P-3C Lockheed Orion anti-submarine planes in both the East China Sea and the Pacific Ocean.

The decision follows the arrest of a record 581 illegal Chinese immigrants by Japanese authorities in the first two months of this year. The number is more than the total for the whole of last year of 545 people.
Many of the illegal immigrants come from Fujian and other densely populated coastal areas of China. They are lured by the prospect of high wages in Japan.
The primary responsibility for seizing the boats and arresting illegal immigrants rests with the coastguard, or the Maritime Safety Agency, the navy spokesman said.
"Our aim is to increase our coverage of the seas to detect suspect boats and notify the Maritime Safety Agency," the navy spokesman said.
The navy conducts 24-hour patrols of the seas around Japan but its primary mission is tracking submarines and other foreign warships.

Last month, Japanese police arrested seven suspected members of a Japan-based Chinese "snakehead" immigrant smuggling ring, the first crackdown on groups suspected to be organising the flow of illegal immigrants.
Japanese police say they are targeting snakehead groups, which are so-called because of their viciousness.
